u-stamford.note: The Victoria County History dates the quarrel and the migration to Stamford to 1334; some accounts give 1333.

u-dublin-stpatricks.note: Wikipedia, citing Newman's Rise and Progress of Universities and the Dictionary of Irish Biography.

a-warrington.note: Wikipedia, citing Parker, Dissenting Academies in England (1914) and Fulton (1933).

u-oxford-1096-founding.note: The university states that teaching existed in some form by 1096; the first named master, Theobald of Étampes, is recorded c.1117.

u-oxford-1214-charter.note: Ordinance of 25 June 1214; a chancellor is first recorded in office c.1221.

u-cambridge-1229-migration.note: Henry III's invitation is documented; how many Paris scholars settled at Cambridge is uncertain.

u-stamford-1333-founding.note: The quarrel between northern and southern scholars and the move to Stamford are dated 1334.

u-oxford-1355-destruction.note: Riot of 10 February 1355; the figure of about 63 scholars killed comes from traditional accounts.

u-cambridge-1381-destruction.note: The destruction of university records in 1381 is documented; the attack on Corpus Christi comes from other accounts.

u-oxford-1571-charter.note: The 1571 Act incorporated both Oxford and Cambridge.

u-cambridge-1856-access.note: The Act removed religious oaths for degrees in arts, law, medicine and music; Senate membership still required Anglican conformity.

u-oxford-1879-access.note: Lady Margaret Hall opened on 16 October 1879.

u-dublin-stpatricks-1320-founding.note: Bicknor's charter of 1320 acted on a papal brief of Clement V usually dated 1311 or 1312.

u-st-andrews-1413-founding.note: Teaching began in 1410 and Bishop Wardlaw granted a charter in 1411.

fix.desc: Bishop James Kennedy founded St Salvator's; St Leonard's (1512) and St Mary's (1537) followed.

u-st-andrews-1450-reform.note: St Mary's College was founded by Archbishop James Beaton in 1537.

u-copenhagen-1479-founding.note: Papal permission dated 19 June 1475; inaugurated in the Church of Our Lady on 1 June 1479.

fix.desc: Papal bull at the request of James IV and Bishop Elphinstone; the first students arrived in 1505.

u-aberdeen-kings-1495-founding.note: The university states that King's College welcomed its first students in 1505.

u-uppsala-1527-confessional.note: The university declined after 1515 and teaching had virtually ceased by about 1530.

u-dublin-stpatricks-1534-suppression.note: The university disappeared during the Irish Reformation, 1534-41.

m-london-gresham-1597-founding.note: Founded in 1597 by Gresham's executors in his Bishopsgate mansion, administered by the City and the Mercers' Company.

u-aberdeen-kings-1641-reform.note: This source dates the union of the two universities from 1640 until after the Restoration.

m-london-gresham-1660-reform.note: The Royal Society met at Gresham College until 1710, but this source dates its incorporation to 1663; the founding meeting after Wren's lecture of November 1660 is not covered.

u-lund-1666-founding.note: Founding documents signed 19 December 1666; inaugurated 28 January 1668.

u-dublin-1689-suppression.note: Tyrconnell's Jacobite government closed the college and used it as a barracks, 1689-91.

u-turku-helsinki-1722-refoundation.note: Teaching was suspended for almost ten years, until after the Peace of Nystad; the exact reopening year is not given in this source.

u-glasgow-1727-reform.note: Regenting, reintroduced in 1642, was ended in 1727.

a-northampton-1729-founding.note: Opened at Market Harborough in early July 1729; moved to Northampton in December 1729.

fix.desc: Founded by royal resolution as the Free Mathematical School (Den frie Mathematiske Skole).

t-christiania-krigsskolen-1750-founding.note: Founded by royal resolution in 1750 as 'Den frie Mathematiske Skole'.

m-london-gresham-1768-relocation.note: The site was sold to the Crown by Act of Parliament.

a-warrington-1783-suppression.note: Teaching ended in 1782 and the academy was formally dissolved in 1786.

t-london-rvc-1791-founding.note: Built in St Pancras in 1791; the first four students began in January 1792. The Odiham Agricultural Society backed Charles Vial de St Bel's plan.

a-hackney-1796-suppression.note: Debts, quarrels among the tutors, the arrest of leading governors and student irreligion brought about its closure.

a-northampton-1798-suppression.note: Closed by the trustees in 1798; reopened at Wymondley in 1799.

u-christiania-1811-founding.note: Opened in 1813 with five professors and 18 students.

t-kongsberg-1814-suppression.note: Jens Esmark moved mining studies to the new university.

t-falun-1819-founding.note: Founded by Charles XIV John; moved to Stockholm in 1868.

t-edinburgh-watt-1821-founding.note: Founded by Leonard Horner and Robert Bryson in Niddry Street.

u-durham-1832-founding.note: The first students came into residence in 1833.

u-durham-1837-charter.note: Charter of 1 June 1837; first degrees conferred a week later.

a-edinburgh-newcollege-1843-founding.note: Founded after the Disruption of 1843 with Chalmers as principal; the November opening and the 1850 Mound building are not covered by these sources.

t-cirencester-1845-founding.note: Royal charter 1845; the first 25 students were admitted in September 1845.

fix.desc: Founded by public subscription with a royal charter from Queen Victoria; the first students arrived in September 1845.

u-belfast-queens-1845-founding.note: Charter dated 30 December 1845; matriculation examinations in October and lectures from 7 November 1849.

u-cork-queens-1845-founding.note: Charter dated 30 December 1845; lectures began 7 November 1849.

a-bessastadir-1846-relocation.note: The school moved into its new Reykjavík building on 1 October 1846.

m-reykjavik-prestaskolinn-1847-founding.note: Merged into the University of Iceland in 1911.

u-london-1849-access.note: Founded by Elizabeth Jesser Reid at 47 Bedford Square; its students took London degrees from the early 1880s.

u-belfast-queens-1850-reform.note: The colleges were linked to the Queen's University from its 1850 charter, but they were incorporated in 1845 and opened in 1849; 1850 marks the university's creation rather than a change at the college.

u-cork-queens-1850-reform.note: Cork's own records treat it as a member college from its 1845 charter; 1850 marks the creation of the Queen's University.

u-galway-queens-1850-reform.note: The colleges were incorporated in 1845 and opened in 1849; 1850 marks the creation of the Queen's University.

u-christiania-1852-relocation.note: Store norske leksikon places the university in Karl Johans gate from 1851; the buildings were completed in 1852.

u-oxford-1854-access.note: Religious subscription was removed at matriculation and for the lower degrees, though colleges kept their own barriers.

t-copenhagen-agri-1856-founding.note: Established by the Act of 8 March 1856.

t-copenhagen-agri-1856-merger.note: The new college was a continuation and expansion of the Veterinary School.

t-dublin-rcs-1867-founding.note: Formed in 1867 from the Museum of Irish Industry at 51 St Stephen's Green, with Robert Kane as dean.

m-maynooth-1869-suppression.note: Compensation was paid on the ending of the grant.

t-coopers-hill-1871-founding.note: Founded in 1870 under the Duke of Argyll; opened in 1871 and closed in 1906.

fix.desc: Opened in the unfinished Castle Hotel building with 25 students under Thomas Charles Edwards.

u-aberystwyth-1872-founding.note: Opened on 16 October 1872; the university records 25 students.

u-copenhagen-1875-access.note: A royal decree of 1875, prompted by Nielsine Nielsen's application, admitted women; she qualified in medicine in 1885.

m-reykjavik-medical-1876-founding.note: Merged into the University of Iceland in 1911.

fix.desc: Reorganised and renamed Kungliga Tekniska högskolan, having absorbed the higher course of the Falun mining school in 1867.

t-stockholm-kth-1877-reform.note: KTH dates the incorporation of the School of Mining to 1867.

u-stockholm-1878-founding.note: The university gives 1878 as its founding year, but says the first public lectures were held in autumn 1877.

u-sheffield-1879-founding.note: Founded by Mark Firth; the royal opening is not covered by this source.

u-birmingham-mason-1880-founding.note: The university dates Mason's foundation to 1875 (foundation stone); teaching began in 1880.

u-lund-1880-access.note: Hildegard Björck and Hedda Andersson were the first women students, in 1880.

u-liverpool-1881-founding.note: Charter of 18 October 1881; opened in January 1882 in former Royal Infirmary buildings beside the medical school.

fix.desc: Chartered on 18 October 1881; teaching began in January 1882 in former Royal Infirmary buildings in the city centre.

u-nottingham-1881-founding.note: Gladstone laid the foundation stone in 1877.

u-belfast-queens-1882-access.note: Women entered the Arts faculty in 1882 and all faculties from 1889.

fix.desc: An 1882 law opened the examen artium to women and Cecilie Thoresen matriculated that year; an 1884 law admitted women to degrees.

u-christiania-1882-access.note: An 1882 law let women take the examen artium; full admission to study and degrees followed in 1884.

u-cardiff-1883-founding.note: Opened 24 October 1883 with 151 students; royal charter 1884.

u-cork-queens-1886-access.note: Five women registered in 1886-87; the college timeline gives 1885.

u-galway-queens-1888-access.note: 1888 is the year of the college's first woman graduate, Bessie Anderson; women were admitted earlier.

a-manchester-1889-relocation.note: New buildings by Thomas Worthington opened in 1893.

u-aberdeen-1892-access.note: The university dates the opening of all its faculties to women to 1894; women became eligible under the 1889 Act's ordinances in 1892.

u-durham-1895-access.note: The supplementary charter was sought in 1895; the first four women matriculated in 1896.

u-birmingham-mason-1897-reform.note: The university dates the change to Mason University College to 1898.

th670.note: Chancellor (head of the schools) c.1215-21 and first lecturer in theology to the Oxford Franciscans c.1229-35.

th671.note: Studied at Oxford c.1228-36, taught in Paris in the 1240s and was again at Oxford c.1248-51; the chronology is uncertain.

th672.note: At Oxford from c.1290; lectured on the Sentences 1298-99 before leaving for Paris in 1302.

th673.note: Lectured on the Sentences at Oxford from 1317 and left for the London Greyfriars c.1321.

th674.note: Master of Balliol c.1360-61; doctor of divinity 1372/73; left Oxford for Lutterworth in 1381.

th677.note: Oxford education confirmed, but not the years or hall.

th679.note: Mostly in London from 1667; deprived of his Christ Church studentship while in exile in 1684.

th686.note: Probably came from Oxford and stayed until 1521.

th690.note: Lucasian professor from 1669; moved to the Mint in London in 1696 and resigned his Cambridge posts in 1701.

th691.note: Lucasian professor 1828-39, though he never lectured.

th694.note: Graduated in 1854; held chairs elsewhere before returning in 1871 as first Cavendish professor.

th696.note: Admitted to Gray's Inn in 1576, bencher 1586 and reader 1587.

th739.note: Entered Glasgow aged 10 (1834); professor of natural philosophy from 1846.

th692.note: Admitted October 1827, in residence from January 1828; BA January 1831.

th698.note: Harvey began the Lumleian lectures in 1616.

th699.note: First Gresham professor of geometry from 1596, leaving in July 1620 for the Savilian chair at Oxford.

th702.note: Ran the academy from 1729 until he left for Lisbon, where he died in October 1751.

th705.note: He was only briefly associated with Hackney between the 1791 riots and his emigration in 1794.

th708.note: Dalton taught at the academy in its early Manchester years.

th711.note: Held the chair 1828-31 and again 1836-66, resigning on principle both times.

th713.note: Studied at UCL until 1854, then spent five years in Australia; professor at UCL from 1876. The span 1851-1880 includes long absences.

th720.note: Lecturer from 1854; dean of the Normal School of Science from 1881.

th722.note: Professor of political economy from 1866; moved to University College in 1876.

th723.note: First professor of engineering at Owens, 1868-1905.

th724.note: Enrolled at Owens College in 1870 and left for Trinity College, Cambridge in 1876.

th730.note: First Regius professor of mathematics at St Andrews, 1668-74.

th731.note: Professor of moral philosophy 1823-28; his student years from 1791 are not covered by this source.

th733.note: His Glasgow chair (1730 inaugural lecture) to his death in 1746 is confirmed; the 1711 start of his studies is not.

th734.note: Studied 1737-40; professor of logic 1751 and of moral philosophy 1752 until 1764.

th736.note: Appointment dated 1757; end date not stated in this source.

th741.note: Appointed to King's College, Aberdeen in 1752.

th746.note: Studied at Edinburgh from about age 11 to 15, roughly 1722-26.

th747.note: Began teaching at Edinburgh on 3 November 1725; died in 1746.

th750.note: Professor at Edinburgh from 1766 until his death in 1799.

th751.note: Held the chair of moral philosophy from 1785 until 1820.

th764.note: Graduated at Trinity; professor 1607-21; Bishop of Meath from 1621.

th766.note: Entered about 1700, fellow 1707, left on becoming Dean of Derry in 1724.

th769.note: Entered Trinity about 1823; appointed Andrews professor of astronomy in 1827 while an undergraduate; died in 1865.

th772.note: Appointed first vice-president and professor of chemistry in 1846; the college opened in 1849.

th774.note: Professor at University College Dublin from 1884 until his death in 1889.

th776.note: Entered Uppsala 1648, professor of medicine from 1660, died 1702.

th778.note: Studied at Uppsala from 1728, abroad 1735-38, professor from 1741 until his death in 1778.

th780.note: Studies interrupted for tutoring; medical degree May 1802.

th782.note: Doctorate 1839 and head of physics from 1858 until death in 1874; the 1833 entry date is not confirmed.

th784.note: Arrived early 1668; the university closed in 1676 and he moved to Stockholm in 1677.

th786.note: Professor of Greek from 1812; appointed Bishop of Växjö in 1824 and moved there in 1826.

th787.note: Professor at the Stockholm surgical school from 1807, which became the Karolinska Institute in 1810; gave up teaching duties in 1832.

th788.note: Privatdocent from 1883, lecturing from early 1884; professor 1889; died February 1891.

th789.note: His appointment in 1881 is confirmed; the end date is not.

th791.note: Entered 19 April 1559; left for Leipzig in February 1562.

th792.note: Professor of anatomy from 1648 and of medicine from 1654; died 1680. A 1646 start is not confirmed.

th793.note: Matriculated 27 November 1656; in Amsterdam by March 1660.

th794.note: Professor of astronomy from 1681, after his years in Paris; died 1710.

th796.note: He finished school in Aarhus in 1800 and graduated in theology at Copenhagen in 1803.

th797.note: Began at the university in 1808; professor of literary history 1825 and of Oriental languages 1831; died 1832.

th799.note: Magister dissertation 1841; entry year not stated in this source.

th800.note: Director from the school's founding until his death in 1851.

th801.note: Lecturer in Danish from 1822 until the academy closed in 1849; head from 1842.

th802.note: Lecturer from 1813 and professor of applied mathematics and astronomy from 1816; stepped down as observatory director in 1861.

th804.note: Entered the university in 1859; extraordinary professor from 1872; at Leipzig 1886-98 before returning.

th805.note: Took the examen artium in 1880 and chose zoology; became curator at Bergen Museum after his 1882 voyage.

th806.note: Taught at Bessastaðir after his 1819 degree and was first rector in Reykjavík from 1846 until 1851.

th807.note: Entered in autumn 1823 and graduated on 10 June 1829.

th808.note: Director of the seminary from 1847 until he became Bishop of Iceland in 1866.

th810.note: Began at Turku in 1745 and studied at Uppsala 1750-51; the 1753 end date is not confirmed.

th812.note: Medical degree 1832 and professor of Finnish 1853-62 are confirmed; for 1833-53 he was a district medical officer in Kajaani, not at the university.

th813.note: Studied at Turku and was lecturer in Latin at Helsinki from 1831 until his move to Porvoo in 1837; the 1822 start is not confirmed here.

th814.note: Instructor in philosophy from 1835 and professor from 1856; a senator from 1863. Continuous residence from 1822 is not confirmed.

th815.note: Became professor of Finnish history in 1864, not 1854, and was rector 1875-78.
